title: Binary Synthetic Template Oligonucleotide Positive Control for RT-PCR
author: Ian M Mackay
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.yxjfxkn
materials: Reconstitute each lyophilised STO DNA to a final concentration of 200µM (equivalent to 200 picomoles per microliter; pmol/µl), in their original tube, using nuclease-free water. Affix a printed label to the tube stating the date of reconstitution and final concentration. Add another label to the STO datasheet as well as reconstitution details, and file. Freeze unused reconstituted STO at -20ºC. In a 200μl (0.2ml) PCR tube, assemble the following reaction mix on the bench at room temperature (only thaw frozen reagents as needed, keep them in a cold brick, then immediately return them to the freezer when finished with them): Incubate the tube in a 96-well conventional thermocycler using with the following conditions: 37ºC 60min 4ºC hold

Stop the thermocycler and remove the tube. To this tube add the following reaction mix on the bench at room temperature (only thaw frozen reagents as needed, keep them in a cold brick, then immediately return them to the freezer when finished with them): Split by transferring 60µl into a new 200μl tube. Incubate both tubes in a 96-well conventional thermocycler using with the following conditions: 37ºC 30min 4ºC hold Remove each tube, add 1µl of TURBO DNase, mix by pipetting, return the tubes to the thermocycler and incubate them using the following cycling conditions: 37ºC 30min 4ºC hold Remove the tubes, combine contents into a fresh 1.5ml tube and add 14µl of thawed DNase Inactivation Reagent (10X) to each 0.2ml tube. Incubate at room temperature for 5min, flicking 2-3 times during incubation Centrifuge at 10,000xg for 1.5min Use a micropipette to carefully transfer the supernatant into a new nuclease-free 1.5ml tube

steps.title: Design synthetic template oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: Create two single‑stranded DNA STOs (PRIMER control and PROBE control) that contain a 5' T7 transcription promoter (or omit for DNA viruses), the virus‑specific primer or probe hybridisation sites, and the non‑viral UBE2D2 primer/probe sites in the correct orientation; each STO should be ~94 nt (PRIMER) or ~106 nt (PROBE).

steps.title: Order and resuspend STO DNA
steps.instruction: Order the designed STOs as dry, purified DNA (e.g., IDT Ultramer, 4 nmol scale) from a supplier different from that used for diagnostic primers/probes, or order the two sets at least one week apart; upon receipt, resuspend each in molecular‑grade water to the concentration supplied by the manufacturer.

steps.title: Aliquot and store undiluted STO RNA
steps.instruction: Divide the undiluted in‑vitro‑transcribed STO RNA into two labelled tubes, measure an optical density on one aliquot, record full storage location details, and store the tubes at –80 °C for long‑term stability.

steps.title: Prepare 10‑fold serial dilution series
steps.instruction: Generate a 10‑fold dilution series from 10⁻² to 10⁻¹¹ using RNase‑free water and pre‑labelled 10 × 2 mL screw‑capped tubes kept on ice.

substeps.instruction: Thaw one vial of STO RNA and label it as thawed.
Add 495 µL RNase‑free water to the first tube and 450 µL to each of the remaining nine tubes.
Transfer 5 µL of undiluted STO RNA into the first tube (495 µL water) to create the 10⁻² dilution; vortex the capped tube with three pulses of 2–5 seconds each.
Return the remaining undiluted stock to the –80 °C freezer.
Transfer 50 µL from the 10⁻² tube into the second tube (450 µL water) to make the 10⁻³ dilution; vortex as above.
Repeat the 50 µL transfer and vortex step sequentially through tubes 3–10, producing dilutions 10⁻⁴ to 10⁻¹¹; discard the final 50 µL after the last transfer.

steps.title: Prepare PCR/RT‑PCR reaction mixes
steps.instruction: Make sufficient master mix to test the entire dilution series in duplicate, include a no‑template control (NTC) and a small excess; for each reaction add the appropriate amount of STO RNA/DNA as if it were a biospecimen extract, and also add the required UBE2D2 primers or probe to complete amplification of the hybrid template.

steps.title: Run duplicate PCR and RT‑PCR assays
steps.instruction: Aliquot the prepared reaction mixes (including each dilution in duplicate, NTC, and excess) into the appropriate tubes, plates or rings for the instrument; run both a specific rPCR (DNA‑only) and an RT‑rPCR (RNA‑reverse‑transcribed) on the dilution series.

steps.title: Analyze results and select routine dilution
steps.instruction: Determine the highest dilution that yields positive amplification in duplicate for DNA (rPCR) and RNA (RT‑rPCR); ensure the last RT‑rPCR‑positive dilution is at least one log10 more dilute than the last rPCR‑positive dilution; for routine use select a dilution (e.g., 10⁻⁶) that gives a sigmoidal curve with Cₜ ≈ 20–25.

steps.title: Store long‑term and working control stocks
steps.instruction: Return the original NEAT STO stocks to –80 °C storage; keep useful working dilutions (e.g., 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁹) at –80 °C; prepare frozen control mix stocks: synPri + UBE2D2 probe + water (PRIMER control) and synPrb + UBE2D2 primers + water (PROBE control), in bulk or single‑use tubes as needed; each diagnostic run must include one tube of each control mix.

steps.title: Prepare high‑throughput control master mixes (optional)
steps.instruction: Adjust each control mix to a final volume of 2.5 µL; prepare bulk virus‑specific oligonucleotide mixes (primers, probes, water) also to 2.5 µL; aliquot and store generic RT‑rPCR/rPCR master mix portions; thaw master mix as needed and combine with the appropriate virus‑specific and control mixes for multiplex runs.

steps.title: Purify RNA using RNeasy kit
steps.instruction: Perform RNA purification at room temperature following the steps below:

substeps.instruction: Add 250 µL 100 % ethanol to the supernatant from the RNA extraction, mix by pipetting up and down, and transfer the entire mixture to an RNeasy spin column.
Transfer the column to a fresh collection tube and discard the old tube.
Add 500 µL Buffer RPE, spin at 10,000 rpm for 15 seconds.
Transfer the column to a fresh collection tube and discard the old tube.
Add another 500 µL Buffer RPE, spin at 10,000 rpm for 2 minutes.
Transfer the column to a fresh collection tube and discard the old tube.
Add 50 µL RNase‑free water to the column, spin at 10,000 rpm for 1 minute to elute the STO RNA.
Transfer the eluate to a labelled screw‑cap tube and store as described in step 3.
